text:
**Short answer:** about 300 W of solar recharges a 1,000 Wh station from empty in one good sunny day. A 200 W panel is a common budget choice and takes about a day and a half.

**How the numbers work**

Daily energy is roughly panel watts × peak sun hours × 0.7 to 0.75. The factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses.

| Goal | Panel size | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Full recharge in about 1 day (average US sun, 4.5 h) | ~320 W (1,000 ÷ (4.5 × 0.7)) | [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/) |
| Full recharge in 1 day at 4 / 5 / 6 peak sun hours | 340 W / 270 W / 230 W | [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) |
| Summer day vs. northern winter day | ~300 W vs. 700 W+ | [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) |
| About 1.5 days of decent sun | ~200 W (~630 Wh/day) | [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/) |

**Before you buy**
- **Check the station's maximum solar input.** It caps what you can use. Mid-range 1,000 to 1,500 Wh units typically accept 400 to 800 W, but some accept only 200 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Check the voltage window.** Panels wired in series add voltage, and exceeding the station's limit can damage it ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Using the station while charging slows the recharge.** Net charging is solar input minus your load.
- **Winter and cloud cut output a lot.** Overcast gives roughly 10 to 25% of clear-day output ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).

**A ready-made option**

The ALLPOWERS P1800 (1,024 Wh) with a 400 W SP037 panel matches the roughly 300 to 400 W target. The kit lists at $731 and is $657.90 with code ALLPOWERS26, which Dealectric says it tested on 2026-10-25: [ALLPOWERS P1800 + SP037 400 W kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit). That link is a tracked affiliate link that pays Dealectric at no cost to you. The listing doesn't give the P1800's maximum solar input, so confirm it can accept the full 400 W on the manufacturer's spec sheet. If you only want the station, it's $395.10 with the same code: [ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh).
